explanation: A Graphical User Interface lets users interact with a computer through icons, windows and menus instead of typed commands.

text: Who is known as the father of the computer?
explanation: Charles Babbage designed the Difference Engine and the Analytical Engine, the first mechanical general-purpose computer concept.

text: The first generation of computers used which component for switching?
explanation: First-generation machines such as ENIAC and UNIVAC relied on vacuum tubes, which were bulky and generated great heat.

text: A compiler differs from an interpreter in that a compiler
options: translates the source program line by line at run time
converts machine code back into source code
executes the program without any translation
translates the entire source program before execution
explanation: A compiler translates the whole source program into object code in one pass, whereas an interpreter translates and executes one statement at a time.

text: An assembler is a program that converts
explanation: An assembler translates mnemonic assembly-language instructions into the binary machine code of a particular processor.

text: The main printed circuit board of a computer to which all other components connect is the
explanation: The motherboard carries the processor socket, memory slots, buses and connectors that link every other component.

text: One byte is equal to how many bits?
explanation: A byte is a group of eight binary digits and is the standard unit used to represent one character of data.

text: One kilobyte is conventionally equal to
explanation: Computer memory is measured in powers of two, so one kilobyte equals 2 to the power 10, that is 1024 bytes.

text: A group of four bits is called a
explanation: Half a byte, that is four bits, is termed a nibble and corresponds to exactly one hexadecimal digit.

text: One terabyte is equal to
explanation: The sequence of binary storage units rises by a factor of 1024, so 1 TB equals 1024 GB.

text: RAM is described as volatile memory because it
options: can only be read and never written
loses its contents when power is switched off
stores data permanently on magnetic platters
is located outside the computer case
explanation: Random Access Memory needs a constant power supply to retain data, so its contents vanish when the machine is switched off.

text: Which of the following memories has the fastest access time?
explanation: Cache memory sits closest to the processor and is built from high-speed static RAM, so it is accessed far faster than any secondary storage.

text: The storage capacity of a standard single-layer DVD is approximately
explanation: A single-sided, single-layer DVD holds about 4.7 gigabytes, roughly seven times the capacity of a CD.

text: Which of the following is an input device?
explanation: A scanner converts printed images and text into digital data and feeds it into the computer, which makes it an input device.

text: OMR technology is chiefly used to read
options: marks made in bubbles on answer sheets
explanation: Optical Mark Recognition detects the presence of pencil marks in fixed positions, which is why it is used to grade multiple-choice answer sheets.

text: OCR in computing stands for
explanation: Optical Character Recognition converts scanned images of printed or typed text into machine-editable characters.

text: Which of the following is an impact printer?
explanation: A dot matrix printer forms characters by striking pins against an inked ribbon and the paper, so it works by physical impact.

text: Which device functions as both an input and an output device?
explanation: A touch screen displays information like a monitor and simultaneously accepts user input through touch, serving both roles.

text: The smallest addressable element of an image on a computer display is called a
explanation: A pixel, short for picture element, is the smallest dot of the display grid whose colour and brightness can be controlled.

text: Printer resolution is normally measured in
explanation: Dots per inch expresses how many separate ink or toner dots a printer can place along one inch, which determines print sharpness.

text: The World Wide Web was invented by
explanation: Tim Berners-Lee proposed and built the World Wide Web at CERN in 1989, creating HTML, HTTP and the first browser.

text: HTTP stands for
explanation: Hypertext Transfer Protocol is the application-layer protocol used by web browsers and servers to exchange web pages.

text: HTML is best described as
options: an operating system for web servers
a markup language for creating web pages
explanation: Hypertext Markup Language uses tags to define the structure and content of web pages displayed by browsers.

text: In the context of the internet, URL stands for
explanation: A Uniform Resource Locator is the complete address that identifies where a resource is located on the web.

text: FTP is a protocol used primarily for
options: transferring files between computers over a network
explanation: File Transfer Protocol defines how files are uploaded to and downloaded from a remote server over a TCP/IP network.

text: SMTP is the standard protocol used for
explanation: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol governs the sending and relaying of email messages between mail servers.

text: LAN stands for
explanation: A Local Area Network connects computers within a limited area such as one office building or campus.

text: The Domain Name System (DNS) performs the function of
options: translating domain names into IP addresses
explanation: DNS acts as the directory of the internet, converting human-readable names such as fpsc.gov.pk into numeric IP addresses.

text: An IPv4 address consists of how many bits?
explanation: IPv4 uses a 32-bit address written as four decimal octets separated by dots, allowing about 4.3 billion addresses.

text: An IPv6 address is how many bits long?
explanation: IPv6 expanded the address space to 128 bits, written as eight groups of hexadecimal digits, to overcome IPv4 exhaustion.

text: The network device used to connect two or more different networks and forward packets between them is a
explanation: A router examines the destination IP address of each packet and chooses the best path to forward it to another network.

text: The word modem is derived from
explanation: A modem modulates digital data onto an analogue carrier for transmission and demodulates the incoming signal back into digital form.

text: The OSI reference model consists of how many layers?
explanation: The Open Systems Interconnection model has seven layers, from the physical layer up to the application layer.

text: Wi-Fi wireless networking is defined by which IEEE standard family?
explanation: The IEEE 802.11 family of standards specifies wireless local area networking, marketed under the name Wi-Fi.

text: Which network is regarded as the forerunner of the modern internet?
explanation: ARPANET, funded by the US Department of Defense in 1969, was the first packet-switching network and evolved into the internet.

text: In a star topology, all the nodes of the network are connected to
explanation: Star topology links every node by its own cable to a central hub or switch, through which all communication passes.

text: The default port number used by HTTPS is
explanation: Secure web traffic over TLS is carried on port 443, while unencrypted HTTP uses port 80.

text: Which file extension belongs to an MS Excel workbook created in Excel 2007 or later?
explanation: Excel 2007 introduced the Open XML workbook format, saved with the .xlsx extension.

text: A file with the extension .pptx is opened by which program?
explanation: The .pptx extension identifies a PowerPoint presentation stored in the Open XML format.

text: In Windows, a file with the extension .exe is a
explanation: An .exe file contains machine instructions that Windows can load and run directly as a program.

text: PDF stands for
explanation: Portable Document Format, developed by Adobe, preserves a document's layout and fonts across different devices and platforms.

text: Which extension indicates a file containing plain unformatted text?
explanation: A .txt file stores only characters with no formatting information, and can be opened by any text editor.

text: The default file extension of a document created in MS Word 2007 and later versions is
explanation: From Word 2007 onward the default save format is Office Open XML, which uses the .docx extension.

text: In MS Excel, every formula entered in a cell must begin with
explanation: Excel recognises an entry as a formula only when it starts with the = sign, otherwise it treats it as text.

text: In MS Excel, a file that contains one or more worksheets is called a
explanation: The Excel document as a whole is a workbook, and each page of rows and columns inside it is a worksheet.

text: In MS Word, the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + Z performs which action?
explanation: Ctrl + Z reverses the most recent action, and repeated presses step further back through the edit history.

text: In MS PowerPoint, pressing the F5 key
options: starts the slide show from the first slide
explanation: F5 launches the presentation in full-screen slide show mode beginning with the first slide.

text: Which MS Office application is a database management program?
explanation: MS Access stores data in related tables and provides queries, forms and reports, making it the Office database program.

text: Which MS Excel function adds all the numbers in a specified range of cells?
explanation: The SUM function returns the arithmetic total of the values in the range supplied as its argument.

text: In an MS Excel worksheet, columns are identified by
explanation: Excel labels columns with letters A, B, C onwards and rows with numbers, so a cell reference such as B4 combines both.

text: The MS Word feature used to produce many personalised letters from a single template and a list of recipients is called
explanation: Mail Merge combines a main document with a data source so that each copy of the letter carries a different name and address.

text: A self-replicating malicious program that spreads across a network without attaching itself to another program is called a
explanation: A worm is standalone malware that copies itself from computer to computer over a network, unlike a virus which needs a host file.

text: A Trojan horse is malware that
options: disguises itself as a useful program to gain entry
physically damages the hard disk platters
duplicates itself endlessly in memory only
explanation: A Trojan appears to be legitimate software and tricks the user into installing it, after which it performs hidden harmful actions.

text: Sending fraudulent emails that appear to come from a bank in order to steal a user's password is called
explanation: Phishing uses deceptive messages that imitate a trusted organisation to persuade victims to reveal login or financial details.

text: A firewall in a computer network is used to
options: increase the clock speed of the processor
control incoming and outgoing network traffic
explanation: A firewall filters traffic against a set of security rules, allowing authorised packets and blocking unauthorised ones.

text: Encryption is the process of converting
options: plaintext into an unreadable coded form
source code into an executable file
explanation: Encryption applies an algorithm and a key to turn readable data into ciphertext that only an authorised holder of the key can decode.

text: Malicious software that locks or encrypts a victim's files and demands payment to restore access is known as
explanation: Ransomware holds data hostage by encrypting it and displays a demand for payment in exchange for the decryption key.

text: Unsolicited bulk email sent to a large number of recipients is called
explanation: Spam is unwanted email sent indiscriminately in bulk, usually for advertising or as a vehicle for scams.

text: A denial of service attack aims to
options: steal encryption keys from a database
alter the domain registration of a website
install a hidden keylogger on every client
make a server or service unavailable to legitimate users
explanation: A DoS attack floods a system with excessive requests or traffic so that genuine users can no longer be served.

text: Two-factor authentication improves security because it requires
options: two different antivirus programs to be installed
the password to be changed twice a year
two independent forms of evidence to verify identity
explanation: Two-factor authentication combines something the user knows with something the user has or is, so a stolen password alone is not enough.

text: A small text file that a website stores on a visitor's computer to remember information about the visit is called a
explanation: Cookies are small data files written by a website to the browser so that preferences and session details persist between visits.

text: RADAR stands for
explanation: RADAR is an acronym for Radio Detection and Ranging, describing its use of radio waves to locate objects and measure distance.

text: SONAR is used mainly to detect objects under water because it employs
explanation: Sound waves travel efficiently through water while radio waves are strongly absorbed, so SONAR uses acoustic pulses and their echoes.

text: LASER stands for
options: Light Absorption by Sequential Emission of Rays
Linear Amplification of Standard Electromagnetic Radiation
Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation
Luminous Alignment of Spectral Energy Rays
explanation: The acronym describes the physical process by which the device produces an intense beam, namely stimulated emission of radiation.

text: Laser light differs from ordinary light chiefly because it is
explanation: The waves in a laser beam are in phase and of a single wavelength, which is why the beam stays narrow over long distances.

text: The operation of a laser depends on which phenomenon?
explanation: Stimulated emission, predicted by Einstein, causes an excited atom to emit a photon identical in phase and direction to the incident photon.

text: Holography, the technique of producing three-dimensional images, requires a source of
explanation: Holograms are recorded by the interference of two beams, which demands the highly coherent light that only a laser provides.

text: Optical fibres transmit light signals over long distances on the principle of
explanation: Light striking the core-cladding boundary beyond the critical angle is reflected entirely back into the core and so travels along the fibre.

text: In an optical fibre, the refractive index of the core compared with that of the cladding is
explanation: The core must be optically denser than the cladding for total internal reflection to occur and confine the light inside the core.

text: The medical instrument used to view internal organs, which relies on optical fibres, is the
explanation: An endoscope uses bundles of optical fibres to carry light into a body cavity and return the image to the observer.

text: The first artificial satellite launched into space was
explanation: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 on 4 October 1957, beginning the space age.

text: The orbital period of a geostationary satellite is approximately
explanation: A geostationary satellite completes one orbit in the same time the Earth takes to rotate once, so it appears fixed above one point.

text: A geostationary satellite orbits at a height of about
explanation: Only at roughly 35,800 km above the equator does the orbital period match the Earth's rotation, keeping the satellite stationary in the sky.

text: The first satellite launched by Pakistan was
explanation: Badr-1, an experimental communications satellite built by SUPARCO, was placed in orbit in July 1990.

text: SUPARCO is the national organisation of Pakistan responsible for
explanation: The Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, established in 1961, runs Pakistan's space and satellite programme.

text: GPS stands for
explanation: The Global Positioning System is a satellite constellation that lets a receiver compute its exact location from timing signals.

text: Nuclear power stations generate electricity from which nuclear process?
explanation: Reactors split heavy nuclei such as uranium-235 in a controlled chain reaction, and the heat released raises steam to drive turbines.

text: Which isotope is the usual fuel for a chain reaction in nuclear reactors?
explanation: Uranium-235 is the naturally occurring isotope that undergoes fission readily with slow neutrons, sustaining a chain reaction.

text: The function of a moderator in a nuclear reactor is to
options: absorb excess neutrons and stop the reaction
remove heat from the reactor core
explanation: Materials such as graphite and heavy water reduce neutron speed so that the neutrons are more likely to cause further fission.

text: Control rods in a nuclear reactor are made of materials such as cadmium and boron because these
options: reflect neutrons back into the core
explanation: Cadmium and boron capture free neutrons, so inserting the rods reduces the number available for fission and slows the reaction.

text: Heavy water used in some nuclear reactors is chemically
explanation: Heavy water is D2O, in which ordinary hydrogen is replaced by its heavier isotope deuterium, making it an efficient moderator.

text: The first nuclear power plant of Pakistan was established at
explanation: The Karachi Nuclear Power Plant, KANUPP, began operating in 1972 and was Pakistan's first commercial nuclear power station.

text: Pakistan carried out its first nuclear tests in May 1998 at
explanation: The tests were conducted in the Ras Koh hills of the Chagai district of Balochistan on 28 May 1998.

text: The double helix structure of DNA was proposed in 1953 by
explanation: Watson and Crick, using X-ray diffraction data, described DNA as two complementary strands wound into a double helix.

text: Dolly, the first mammal cloned from an adult body cell, was a
explanation: Dolly the sheep was produced at the Roslin Institute in 1996 by transferring the nucleus of an adult udder cell into an egg cell.

text: The polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is a technique used to
explanation: PCR uses repeated heating and cooling cycles with a DNA polymerase to make millions of copies of a chosen DNA segment.

text: In genetic engineering, restriction enzymes are described as molecular scissors because they
options: cut DNA at specific base sequences
explanation: Each restriction endonuclease recognises a particular short sequence and cuts the DNA there, allowing genes to be isolated.

text: Human insulin for the treatment of diabetes is now produced commercially by
options: chemical synthesis from amino acids in bulk
explanation: The human insulin gene is inserted into bacteria such as E. coli, which then manufacture the hormone by recombinant DNA technology.

text: Tissue culture is a biotechnological technique in which
options: whole plants are grown from small pieces of tissue in a nutrient medium
animal organs are preserved by freezing
soil bacteria are counted under a microscope
seeds are treated with radiation before sowing
explanation: Explants are grown aseptically on a nutrient medium containing hormones, producing many genetically identical plants from one parent.

text: The Human Genome Project was undertaken to
options: determine the complete sequence of human DNA
eliminate all inherited diseases by surgery
map the human nervous system in three dimensions
explanation: The project, declared complete in 2003, identified the sequence of the roughly three billion base pairs in human DNA.

text: Crops carrying a gene transferred from another species are commonly known as
explanation: Transgenic or genetically modified crops such as Bt cotton contain a gene introduced from an unrelated organism by recombinant DNA methods.

text: Which storage device stores data using no moving mechanical parts?
explanation: A solid state drive records data in flash memory chips, so it has no spinning platters or read-write heads.

text: The process of starting a computer and loading the operating system into memory is called
explanation: Booting is the start-up sequence in which firmware tests the hardware and then loads the operating system from storage into RAM.

text: Remote sensing satellites are used chiefly to
options: collect information about the Earth's surface from orbit
measure cosmic rays beyond the solar system
explanation: Remote sensing satellites carry cameras and sensors that record land use, crops, forests and other surface features from orbit.

text: The device that supplies power to a computer for a short time during a mains failure is a
explanation: A UPS holds a battery that takes over instantly when mains power fails, giving time to save work and shut down safely.
